newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Financial squeeze pushes Venezuela interbank trade.
newsitem.headline: Financial squeeze pushes Venezuela interbank trade.

text.p: A continuing liquidity squeeze in Venezuelan financial markets pushed turnover on the interbank lending market above 50 billion bolivars ($103 million) on Tuesday, the Central Bank said.
Interest rates also soared to between 25.0 and 90.0 percent Tuesday for an average of 65 percent as Venezuelan banks struggled to borrow bolivars in a liquidity crunch that began in late May.
It was the first time the Central Bank had revealed turnover on the market, which reached 49 billion bolivars on Monday at an average 10.3 percent lending rate, the Bank said.
Traders welcomed the Bank's move to make the information public.
"It makes the market more transparent. Liquidity is currently in only a few hands, so it helps the rest know better at what rate we should borrow," said one trader.

Unconfirmed reports in daily newspaper El Nacional said Wednesday the on-going liquidity squeeze forced banks in late May to use their reserve requirements deposited with the Central Bank to cover payments.

Analysts say the market tightness, which has seen interbank lending rates go back and forth between five and 95 percent for the past two to three weeks, is partly due to large Central Bank open market operations aimed at mopping-up liquidity to keep inflation down.
Wednesday will see the Bank place 140 billion bolivars of TEMs in its regular auction as around 115 billion bolivars worth of paper expires.
